intro: One scoop of kari ayam (a piece of chicken with gravy) is about 250 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the chicken and the rich coconut milk gravy.

variants.name: Kari ayam with kuah banjir over rice
Kari ayam without santan (using low-fat evaporated milk or yogurt)

diet: Yes, you can. Kari ayam still gives you good protein. What makes the calories jump is lots of coconut gravy poured over rice. Take the chicken piece and just a little gravy, and it still fits your diet. Usually the issue is the rice and kuah banjir, not the chicken.
tips: Take the chicken piece with one or two spoons of gravy, no banjir.
Remove the chicken skin and the oil floating on top of the gravy.
Cooking at home? Use half the santan and top up with water or low-fat evaporated milk.

swap.name: Ayam masak kicap (less oil) or ayam tandoori
swap.why: Less santan and oil, protein still high. You still get that spiced flavour.

faq.q: What's the difference between Malay chicken curry and mamak curry?
faq.a: Malay curry usually uses more santan and tastes richer and sweeter. Mamak curry is heavier on spices and sometimes uses milk or yogurt.

faq.q: Why does curry taste better the next day?
faq.a: The spices and santan soak deeper into the chicken overnight. Keep it in the fridge and reheat until boiling before eating.

faq.q: Can I make kari ayam without santan?
faq.a: Yes. Use low-fat evaporated milk, yogurt or a little milk powder instead. It's lighter but still tasty.
